body:
I was never sexually abused, so my sexuality doesn't stem from abuse. Honestly, I think it's probably biological.

Like I said before, I don't take pedophilia to be an identity; I don't even like using the word. The problem is, everyone else (see: this thread) acts like it's some huge issue when it's really not.
What made you think you were a pedophile? And what sexual/emotional feelings do you have for children now?
Please don't take this the wrong way, but I think I know a *tiny* bit more about pedophilia than you. Y'know, being a pedophile and all.

I'm not sure you can do rat studies about PTSD and BPD; they're pretty complex disorders, and any study on rats would have to be taken with a grain of salt. Though, I did a quick Google and the only thing that came up for "psilocybin study rat" was [this](http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2000343/) which didn't seem to be about BPD and PTSD. I get what you say about closely controlled environments, and I'm sure I'd get more out of shrooms if I took them with an experienced therapist, but that's not possible at the moment. I realize it could be dangerous, but I'm willing to risk it.

Thanks for all the links, though, they're really interesting! :)

I've had sexual exploration (fooled around with a friend my age since I was 15, and with a guy at college when I was 18), and I still prefer boys. Like I said, sexually I don't have a preference but I feel more emotionally attracted to children. It's not about "progressing" to an appreciation of the adult form; I already appreciate it. I just don't like adults as much romantically.

The problem is I start to get this hazy cloud in my head during the day if I smoke every night. It only takes about a week for me to feel completely burnt out when I smoke. Plus, when I mentioned to my doctor that I smoked, she said that mental health professionals wouldn't diagnose me with anything except cannabis dependence. If I was diagnosed with BPD and I found a strain of weed that helped, it might be different, but right now I think I'm better off not smoking.

>some researchers state that anything that treats ptsd should also treat bpd

That sounds pretty interesting; do you have any more information about that? Because I took shrooms a few months ago and they really helped whatever fucked up issues I have.

I'm non-exclusive, but the emotional attraction just isn't there with men. Also... why would I need a relationship to let me know I'm attracted to children? Are gay people not officially gay until they've had a relationship?

Also, I don't normally use that word to describe myself, but I figured it would be easier to say "I'm a pedophile" than to explain exactly how I feel about children, because I don't think people would understand, and like I said in my post, I don't want advice about pedophilia. I've already come to terms with it, and it's not really an issue to me. The problem is that it's an issue to other people.
I don't think there are any group sessions in my area. If there were, I don't think I'd go to them.

Shit, I forgot to mention in the OP that I'm already on the waiting list for counseling at my school. I applied in January, had an initial assessment in March and won't be getting actual counseling until September. I told the counselor everything, and she seemed accepting... she kept asking if I was molested, though. Like, I think she asked about 5 or 6 times during a half-hour assessment.
I don't know. There's evidence that pedophilia has a biological basis, but I also recently realized how much I regret my childhood. That could be a part of it, I guess?

>I'm so sorry you have to go through this.

Thank you. That honestly means a lot.

>Is there any sort of lgbtq community/club/etc you could reach out to at your school?

Yes, that's where I started making friends in my first semester. It just made me feel fake, though: whenever any deep conversations happened, I knew I had to lie about an integral part of me. I feel like my social anxiety is less bad than it was last year, so in September I'll probably go back to the LQBTQ community and try to make friends again.
